title: The Zarankiewicz number z(13, 19; 3, 3) equals 120: a certified proof
description:
We prove that the Zarankiewicz number z(13, 19; 3, 3) — the largest number of ones in a 13 × 19 0/1 matrix with no 3 × 3 submatrix of ones — equals 120. Matrices with 120 ones were known; the best published upper bound was 122.

The proof is computer-assisted and certified throughout: a counting argument leaves 30 column-degree profiles; 26 are refuted by SAT with DRAT proofs; the four most uniform profiles are split into 2 478 anchor cubes and 58 186 sub-cubes, each refuted either by an exact rational Farkas certificate for a linear relaxation (32 602) or by SAT with a DRAT or LRAT proof. The record contains the research note, the generator and checkers, every certificate record with the SHA-256 of its formula, all Farkas certificates, the audit logs, the witness matrices and a standalone verifier. The DRAT proofs of the 26 whole profiles and of the 12 × 18 link are included (3.4 GB); those of the cubes and sub-cubes (577 GB) are available from the author on request. It also documents a soundness gap in drat-trim's lrat-check (an empty clause with no conflict is accepted) and the strict variant used.

In addition, the record includes explicit witness matrices establishing certified lower bounds for 18 adjacent cells (for instance z(14,23) ≥ 146, z(15,22) ≥ 150, z(15,23) ≥ 156), found independently, reproducing the best bounds of Norris and Borsik and exceeding those of Bhan–Nobili–Langer and Saurabh.
notes: This work was a test task for AperioBot, an add-on for AI agents created by the author, a lawyer at the Aperio Bar Association. AI assistance is disclosed in Section 9 of the research note. The repository also holds witness matrices for 18 neighbouring cells.
